source.statement: Decision EA-009-STEP-STYLES-2026-11-20 resolves the recorded Step open questions. Alphabetic is bijective spreadsheet-style base 26 (1 -> A, 26 -> Z, 27 -> AA, 703 -> AAA) in both casings; Roman is greedy subtractive with the standard 13-symbol table in both casings and no 3999 cap (4000 -> MMMM); non-positive values render as plain decimal digits in every style; reset affects only future allocation (existing steps keep their labels, the next allocated value is the explicit start again); the explicit start is a floor bounded 1..10 and the next allocation is max(highest non-retired value + 1, start) so existing larger values force continuation; values stay stable after deletion, reorder, undo, redo and reload as the SPEC requires, a deliberate contract-mandated divergence from ShareX's renumber-on-delete. Mapping sources: ShareX StepTypeFormatter (ShareX.ImageEditor/Core/Annotations/StepType.cs, matched case for case) for the letters, Roman table and the value <= 0 guard. Reset source: Snagit's Step Tool tutorial Restart Sequence ('restart the lettering or numbering sequence for the next step added to the Canvas', techsmith.com/learn/tutorials/snagit/step). The native candidate code and tests already implement exactly these semantics, so no runtime behavior changes; the decision publishes the capability's first machine-readable test-vectors.json (20 step-format and step-allocation vectors running the production helpers through the Linux conformance adapter; red against the pre-change adapter's unsupported-capability answer, 20/20 after) with the same semantics asserted natively in AnnotationShapesTest. The other fifteen packages carry forward to contract 0.4.3 unchanged in normative text from 0.4.2, where the 2026-11-20 CORE-015 record approved them; the deciding agent verified that carry-forward by inspecting this commit's diff, which touches no other capability package. EA-008's separate Text-border geometry question is explicitly not decided here. No ROOT constitution rule is changed.
